units.title: Fog set to linger as ferries slow down
units.author: courier
units.text: Forecasters expect fog to settle over the Marrow Sound tonight and stay for several days, as a slow-moving area of high pressure keeps the wind away. The Met Office has issued an advisory for the Sound and the coast road, warning that visibility could drop below 50 metres in places.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines said its vessels would run under restricted-visibility procedure, which means lower speeds, extra lookouts and regular sound signals. A spokesperson said the timetable would stay in force but warned commuters from Lisle to expect late arrivals in Port Ammet on most mornings this week.

units.author: courier
units.text: Fog weeks are not unusual in late autumn. Older readers will remember the long fog of thirty-odd winters ago, when the Lisle school closed for four days because the teachers could not get across. The ferry company says its radar has improved a great deal since then.

units.author: courier
units.text: Drivers are asked to slow down on the coast road between Port Ammet and Gilliver, where the verges are unlit for long stretches. Police said they attended two minor collisions in mist yesterday morning, neither of which caused injury. Both involved vehicles following too closely.

units.title: Work boats busy on the Gilliver run as Holm clearance begins
units.author: courier
units.text: Gilliver harbour has seen more traffic than usual this week as supply boats shuttle to Kittering Holm, the uninhabited island 9 km offshore where a contractor has started clearing the forest. The work follows a council decision on a total vegetation clearance, determined under delegated powers earlier this autumn.

units.author: courier
units.text: Grieve Land Services, the Port Ammet firm carrying out the work, confirmed that a crew is living on the island in a temporary camp for the length of the contract. It declined to say how long that is, describing the job as a large but routine clearance and referring further questions to its client.

units.author: courier
units.text: The client, Ardent Vale Holdings, bought the Holm about eighteen months ago. In a short statement the company said it was a patient and responsible owner with a long-term vision for the island and had no further plans to announce at this time. It did not answer a question about what the island would be used for.

units.author: courier
units.text: In Gilliver, opinion on the quayside was mixed. One creel fisherman said the boats were good business for the fuel berth. A woman walking her dog said she was sorry to lose the view of the trees, which she had looked at every morning for sixty years, but supposed someone owned them.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Holm has no road, no mains power and no permanent residents. Historians note it was logged once before, in the 1890s, when a timber camp operated there for part of a season. The island has been left largely to itself for most of the century since.

units.title: Live: fog and travel across the Sound
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 06:45 ST. Good morning. Mist is sitting on the water this morning rather than on the roads, so for now the coast road is clear, but the first ferry from Port Ammet has left 25 minutes late. We will keep this page updated through the day as the fog is expected to thicken this evening.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:20 ST. A listener in Lisle says the queue for the 07:30 sailing goes back past the newsagent. Sound Lines says that sailing will call at Lisle as normal but may be ten minutes behind. Meanwhile the Tollinby school bus is running on time.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:05 ST. Power cut in Port Ammet north this morning is fixed. Sound Power says a bird hit the line on Hythe Road just after six. Several listeners text in to say their alarm clocks are now flashing. Ours too.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 09:10 ST. Planned power work in Tollinby has begun on schedule around Mill Lane. Traders on the east side of the market square say they were told in advance and have brought flasks. The work is due to finish at one o'clock.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:30 ST. The Met Office has confirmed the fog advisory from six this evening. Its forecaster tells us this looks like advection fog, warm moist air moving over cold sea, which tends to be persistent. Expect it on the coast tonight and inland by morning.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 17:45 ST. Fog arriving early in Gilliver. A listener on Harbour Road says she can no longer see the end of the slipway from her window. Sound Lines has warned of delays on all evening crossings and asks foot passengers to wait in the shelters.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 19:30 ST. Carrow Point fog signal now sounding. Several listeners on the headland have messaged to ask how long it will go on. The honest answer is as long as the fog does. That is it from the day desk; the overnight team will pick up anything urgent.

units.title: Dellow Court residents face the stairs again as lift waits for part
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of Dellow Court, the fourteen-storey block off Canal Street, have been using the stairs for much of the week after the building's single lift broke down again. The managing agent, Kerrow Estates, said an engineer had diagnosed a faulty door controller and a replacement part was on order.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Several residents told the Post the lift problem had been made worse by lighting faults in the stairwell between the sixth and eighth floors, where timed lights have been going out early. One retired resident on the seventh floor said she now carries a torch to take her rubbish down.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said it thanked residents for their patience and that lighting faults reported through the proper channel would be logged and investigated. The residents' association said it would raise both issues at its next meeting, which it hopes to hold within the week.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Dellow Court was built in the late 1960s as part of the canal-side redevelopment and has around 150 flats. It has had three lift failures in the past year. The council says the building is privately managed and that enforcement would only follow a formal complaint about safety.

units.title: Thirty days, one island: inside a high-speed clearance contract
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Most clearance contracts in the northern districts run to a season. The Kittering Holm job, awarded to Grieve Land Services, gives a small live-in crew thirty days to clear the island's forest entirely. Industry observers say the timescale is ambitious but not unheard of for a firm prepared to pay for it.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: According to people familiar with the tender, the rate is $100 a tree plus a daily rate per worker, a structure that rewards speed and puts pressure on the site lead to keep saws running in all weather. One contractor called it 'a sprint priced like a marathon'. Grieve did not comment on the figures.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Live-in camps are less common than they were. Most firms now prefer to ferry crews daily, but a 9 km crossing in autumn makes that impractical. The Holm camp is understood to be a converted camper with bunks and a generator, resupplied by boat from Gilliver.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The weather is the obvious risk. A fog week can stop supply boats, and short daylight limits safe felling hours. Health and safety advisers point out that fatigue on long contracts is the single largest cause of chainsaw injuries, and that remote sites need a clear evacuation plan.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Timber merchants in Weyhaven say they have not been approached to buy the Holm's wood, which suggests the client is more interested in the cleared land than the timber. What Ardent Vale Holdings intends for that land has not been made public.

units.title: Tollinby traders brace for a quiet winter
units.author: courier
units.text: Stallholders at Tollinby's twice-weekly market say footfall has fallen since the bus timetable was trimmed in the summer. A cheese seller who has traded there for nineteen years said she now takes home a third of what she brings. Several traders want the council to reinstate the late afternoon bus from Brackwater.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council said the timetable is set by the operator and that it had passed on the traders' concerns. A spokesperson added that free parking on market days would continue until the new year. Traders said parking was not the problem, since most of their regular customers no longer drive.

units.author: courier
units.text: Today's market went ahead despite this morning's planned power cut on the east side of the square. The fish van, which has its own generator, reported its best morning in a month, as shoppers queued beside it to keep warm by the exhaust.

units.title: Coastguard guides lost kayakers home in mist
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Two kayakers who lost their way in mist off Lisle this afternoon were guided back to shore by the coastguard. The pair, both experienced, said the mist came down within ten minutes and they could no longer see the island. They called for help by radio and followed instructions to paddle toward a sound signal.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: A coastguard officer said the kayakers had done everything right by carrying a radio and calling early. He urged anyone thinking of going out on the Sound this week to stay ashore, adding that fog over still water can make sounds seem to come from the wrong direction.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Neither kayaker needed medical treatment. One told Sound FM the strangest part was how quiet it became, with no gulls and no engines, only the drip off their paddles. They said they would be sticking to the reservoir at Brackwater for the rest of the season.

units.title: Gilliver boats stay tied up as fog closes the harbour mouth
units.author: courier
units.text: Most of Gilliver's small fishing fleet stayed in harbour for a second day as fog lay thick across the approach. Creel men said they had missed two hauls and some gear had drifted after markers were lost. The harbour office has been taking reports of missing buoys.

units.author: courier
units.text: The approach buoy that marks the harbour entrance has been unlit since early in the week, which harbour users say has made matters worse. The coastguard says a repair boat will go out as soon as conditions allow. In the meantime, boats are relying on radar and local knowledge.

units.author: courier
units.text: The supply boats running to Kittering Holm have kept to a reduced schedule. A Gilliver skipper said the crossing was manageable with radar but slow, and that unloading at the island's landing beach was the hardest part when you could not see the trees from the water.

units.author: courier
units.text: Four street lights on Harbour Road have also failed after a cable fault, leaving the walk between the chandlery and the slipway dark. Residents have asked for a temporary light. The power co-op says the council's lighting contractor has been called and should attend within days.

units.title: Live: second morning of fog
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 06:30 ST. Fog everywhere this morning. The 06:20 sailing from Lisle is cancelled because the slip is under the ferry's visibility limit. Passengers can use the 07:30. Coast road visibility around 60 metres near Gilliver, slightly better toward Port Ammet.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:05 ST. Overnight there were more delays than usual on the late crossings. Sound Lines says the night boat waited off Gilliver for some time while visibility improved. It has not given further details. The first freight run has also been put back by an hour.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:50 ST. Tollinby and Brackwater schools are open. The Brackwater head says buses may arrive late and no one will be marked absent for it. A listener says the reservoir road is slippery in patches where the fog has frozen on the surface.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:40 ST. Lisle Road in Port Ammet will be closed from half nine for a burst water main. Diversion via Ferry Lane. If you are heading for the ferry terminal, give yourself an extra ten minutes or walk from the bus station.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:15 ST. Brief brightening in Port Ammet, where you can see the harbour wall again. Not so in Gilliver, where our reporter says the fog has not moved at all. The Met Office says don't get used to the sunshine.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 17:20 ST. Freezing fog warning for the Brackwater valley tonight. Gritters are due out from eight. The power co-op says this morning's transformer work on Reservoir Lane finished on time and the visitor car park lights are back on.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 19:40 ST. Ferry delays of 20 to 40 minutes expected tonight. The last Gilliver departure will wait for passengers off the Lisle bus if it is held up. Thank you for all your messages today, especially the photographs of very grey things.

units.title: Letters: the Holm, the bus and the bins
units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, I have watched the boats going out to Kittering Holm all week and I would like to know who decided we should lose an entire forest without a public meeting. The council tells me it was decided under delegated powers. I have lived on this coast for seventy years and I was never delegated anything. Name and address supplied, Gilliver.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, your correspondents worry about trees on an island none of them have set foot on. The Holm is private land, the owner has permission, and a local firm has the work. I would rather the Courier spent its ink on the late afternoon bus from Brackwater, which has not run since July. Name and address supplied, Tollinby.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, for the third week running the recycling on Rope Walk has not been collected on the advertised day. The council newsletter cheerfully reports a vehicle under repair. I have repaired vehicles. It does not take three weeks. Bernard, Rope Walk, Port Ammet.

units.title: Fog slows container port as cranes stand idle
units.author: weypost
units.text: Crane operations at Weyhaven's container terminal were suspended for several hours overnight as fog drifted up the estuary from the Sound. Port managers said visibility at the quay fell below the safe working limit for lifting, leaving two vessels waiting at their berths until mid-morning.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Hauliers queuing at the terminal gate said they had been told to wait in their cabs with engines off. One driver said he had slept four hours in the lay-by and still not moved. The port said it would extend gate hours this evening to clear the backlog.

units.author: weypost
units.text: City bus services ran mostly on time, though the canal-side routes were slowed by roadworks rather than weather. The council reminded drivers that fog lights should be switched off once visibility improves, after complaints about dazzle on the ring road.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Forecasters say the fog could last into next week. A meteorologist at the regional office said the city usually escapes the worst of Sound fog, but the estuary channels it inland on nights like these, which is why the port and the canal streets are often the last places to clear.

units.title: Lost days: what a fog week costs coastal contractors
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: For contractors working on islands and coastal sites, fog is less a hazard than a bill. Every day a supply boat cannot run is a day of fuel, food and parts that has to be found another way. Firms with live-in crews usually build a buffer of a week's supplies into their planning for exactly this reason.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Felling in fog is permitted but slow. Crews must be able to see the drop zone and each other, and many firms set a minimum visibility below which saws stop. On piece-rate contracts that creates an obvious tension, and safety advisers warn that the temptation to push on is strongest in the first week.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Marine logistics firms in the Sound report delays of up to two hours on charter runs this week. One operator said fog itself was manageable with radar but landing on unimproved beaches was not, and that crews on the receiving end were often waiting in the cold without knowing when the boat would appear.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Insurers have their own view. Most standard contractor policies treat weather delays as a business risk rather than an insured event, so the cost falls on the firm or, depending on the contract, on the client. Brokers advise checking the small print before a long remote job.

units.title: Council shortens library hours for winter
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Libraries in Tollinby and Port Ammet will close an hour earlier on weekdays from next week. The council says the change saves money on heating and staff overtime during the darker months. Saturday hours stay as they are and the mobile library will keep its fortnightly visits.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: A part-time assistant at Tollinby library told Sound FM the last hour is when students and shift workers come in, and that the change would hit them hardest. The council said it would review the hours in spring. A petition started this afternoon had 140 signatures by teatime.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The library service also confirmed it will continue to lend reading lamps and radios to housebound readers through the winter. A spokesperson said demand had grown, particularly in Gilliver and Lisle, and that the scheme relied on donations of working equipment.

units.title: Gritters out as freezing fog grips Brackwater valley
units.author: courier
units.text: Council gritting lorries will treat the reservoir road and Brackwater village streets tonight after forecasters warned of freezing fog in the valley. The reservoir car park, popular with walkers and dog owners, will stay open but its access road has not been treated before and may be icy.

units.author: courier
units.text: The estate ranger at the reservoir asked visitors not to walk the woodland paths after dark during the fog. He said the paths are not lit, the ground near the outflow is steep, and recent night visits by people with recording equipment had left gates open that should be closed.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents on Reservoir Lane lost power for two hours this morning while a transformer was replaced. Most had been warned by letter. One said the bigger problem was the junction on the Tollinby road, where temporary traffic lights have now been in place for longer than anyone can remember.
